pool.text: Great Britain officially abolished the slave trade by law in this year.
HMS Comus sailed into Duke Town and captured seven slave ships.
Scottish Presbyterians established a new mission station located within Calabar.
Queen Victoria signed a protection treaty with the king and chiefs.
The National Museum of Calabar was flat packed and shipped from Britain.
The Hope Waddell Training Institution was founded in the city.
St Margaret's Hospital was founded as the first public hospital in Nigeria.
The seat of European government administration was moved to Lagos.
A mail steamer of the Liverpool Elder-Dempster Line called at Calabar.
British governor Clifford established the Legislative Council during this year.
Governor Graeme Thomson attempted to introduce a poll tax in southeast Nigeria.
The historic building officially became designated as a national monument.
Tensions increased between the North and South areas of the country after independence.
The Southeastern area declared itself independent as the Republic of Biafra.
A Nigerian Navy armada left Bonny on a naval campaign towards Calabar.
The former took over the facilities belonging to St Margaret's Hospital.
President Shagari officially inaugurated the Margaret Ekpo International Airport.
The Drill Rehabilitation Centre nature reserve was founded for primates.
Governor Donald Duke initiated the famous Calabar Carnival to advance tourism.
Both LGAs together had an estimated population of 571,500 people.
